This fund is an absolute monster.

So many assumptions are made on the dividend growing.  How long will that last. This year's growth is way below the 10% everyone quotes. I agree SCHD is a great dividend fund, but past results are not indicitive of future results.

Didn't it mention inflation? The video gives a nominal number. With an average of 3% inflation, you'll end up with 100k, equivalent to a 40k yearly income in today's purchasing power.
So what do you have to pay taxes on those dividends if you take it out?
Still pay taxes without taking out
3.24% yield can’t even offset inflation.

Many many people can’t or don’t want to grasp what “cost to yield” is. A stock that pays a 3% dividend and the stock value goes up every year can be a great investment.  Warren Buffett did this with Coke in 1988.  Coke has paid a crummy 3% dividend forever but the stock price has slowly go up forever. Result: Buffet buys Coke for 1.8 billion dollars and each year pays around 3% of Cokes value.  Today Buffett’s Coke is worth 37 Billion and the crummy 3% dividend is $848 million a year.  His ORIGINAL cost to yield % is 63%.   But the average YouTuber only will focus on the crummy present 3 % interest rate and not what you paid vs dividends received today .  Cost of yield.
Hope you fact check this.  The SCHD selection formula is genus and so is Buffett. Good luck.😊
Look at the track record don’t forget appreciation
I have a high yield savings account that pays 4.99%
@24-7games That’s short term plus inflation is like 3% or 4% leaving you 2 or 1% spread. Every market drop people fly to this kind of accounts an miss out on market gains

$100k of SCHD pays about $245 per month ($737 per quarter)
This is only about a quarter of a percent of interest per month. (about 3% per year) That is a ridiculously small amount.

Holding perhaps 10-15% of your portfolio in SCHD is okay, but any more than that, and you are leaving a lot of cash on the table.

Trading options, you should be able to easily make 15% per year. Even leaving the cash in a Capital one or in Fidelity SPAXX will yield more interest per year.

Holding SCHD for potential growth of the ETF is okay, but holding it for the dividend is not worth the time.
options way more risky

@robertswift6101 All stock investing is risky. Any ticker could fall 10% or more in a single day. You may as well try to maximize your return on basically, the same amount of risk.

If you own a stock, you may as well sell covered calls against the shares and make a little extra bucks off them. For Puts, only select stocks you are trying to own, and use a strike 3-5% under the current price. if you get assigned, you got the shares at a discount, if not, you made the premium.

As long as you are only trading options on stocks you want to own, the risk is actually minimal.

Now, if you start chasing big premiums, and trading options on crappy companies, then you are right, folks tend to get stuck on more trades than they win.

If you deposit 100k today and never add another dollar you will double your total fund value and dividend payout every 5 to 10 years.  

3% doesn't sound like much but when you include the 10% growth pushing it up every year that number is huge.  Just do the math , SCHD is a monster!!!
